sections.h2: How an eviction starts in Michigan
sections.html:
No Michigan landlord may remove a tenant without the court. The landlord serves a written notice, waits out the notice period, and then files a summary proceeding in district court. For unpaid rent the notice is a written demand for possession, and the tenant has 7 days from service to pay or leave (MCL 600.5714(1)(a)).

The statute sets short clocks for these cases, counted in days. An owner planning a sale feels them directly, since the court calendar decides when the keys can change hands.

The landlord-tenant statute states the rent rule too: when a tenant neglects or refuses to pay rent, the landlord may end the tenancy with a written 7-day notice to quit (MCL 554.134(2)).

sections.h2: Notices that come before a case is filed
sections.html:
Each notice ties to a different reason for ending the tenancy. The notice has to match the ground the landlord relies on, so sending the wrong one can cost time.

  • Unpaid rent: a written demand for possession, 7 days to pay or leave.
  • Controlled substance clause: a 24-hour written demand, but only where a formal police report has been filed.
  • Threat or injury to a person on the landlord's property: a 7-day written notice to quit, again tied to a police notification.
  • Serious health hazard or extensive damage discovered within 90 days before filing: a 7-day demand to hand back possession or repair.
  • Tenancy at will or by sufferance: one month's notice, or a notice equal to the rent interval if rent is paid more often than every 3 months.
  • Year-to-year tenancy: a notice to quit that ends the lease one year after service.

These grounds come from MCL 600.5714 and MCL 554.134. A tenant who stays after a lease ends under its own terms or by law also falls under summary proceedings.

sections.h2: How to deliver a rent demand
sections.html:
There are four accepted ways: hand it to the tenant, give it to a household member old enough to accept it, mail it by first class mail, or send it by email when the tenant agreed in writing and replied to a confirming message. The demand must describe the rental, state the rent owed, say the tenant has seven days, and show the landlord's address and the notice date.

Taping a notice to the door, sliding it under the door, or mailing it by a method that needs a signature are examples of improper service. If service was done wrong, restart the clock with a fresh demand before you file anything.

sections.h2: What happens once the landlord files
sections.html:
After filing, the court issues a summons. Under the standard rule in MCL 600.5735, trial is set within 10 days of issuance and the summons must be served at least 3 days before trial. A court may adopt a local rule that sets appearance 5 days after service instead. The hearing is to happen within 7 days after the appearance or trial date, and it can be pushed back further only by stipulation of the parties or on the record.

For unpaid rent the landlord has to show three things: the rent wasn't paid, a proper demand was served, and the tenant neither paid nor left within the seven days. A tenant may answer that the rent was paid, ask for a rent reduction for poor repair, or file a counterclaim for repair costs.

A tenant can also apply for rental assistance before the first court date or within 5 days after it. With proof of the application filed and served, the case is paused for 14 days and can be extended once for another 14. If you're selling, allow up to four extra weeks when assistance is pending.

Usually the writ waits 10 days after the judgment for possession. That is the default under MCL 600.5744(5), and it matches the 10 days a tenant gets to pay or move out after a rent judgment.

The statute carves out faster paths. A writ can issue right after judgment, on conditions the court sets, when a unit was ordered vacated for lacking a required certificate of compliance, when entry was forcible or possession is held by force, when the occupant is a trespasser, when a serious health hazard or continuing damage is proven, or in the controlled substance case.

Slower paths exist too. After a land contract forfeiture, no writ issues for 90 days if less than half the price was paid, or for 6 months if half or more was paid. In rent cases, paying the judgment amount and taxed costs inside the window stops the writ. When the writ is carried out, the officer removes occupants and belongings and either leaves the belongings in an area open to the public or delivers them to the sheriff.

sections.h2: Can an owner change the locks or cut utilities to speed things up?
sections.html:
No. MCL 600.2918 makes it unlawful for an owner to interfere with a tenant's possession by force or threat, by removing or keeping the tenant's belongings, by changing locks without handing over keys, by boarding up, by removing doors or windows, or by shutting off heat, water, or electric service the landlord must supply.

A tenant who proves interference can recover actual damages or $200, whichever is greater, for each occurrence, and can recover possession if it was lost. A person forced out in a forcible and unlawful manner can recover three times actual damages or $200, whichever is greater. These rights can't be waived in a lease.

The owner is protected when acting under a court order, when making needed repairs or inspections as the law allows, or when in good faith believing the tenant has abandoned the home after diligent inquiry and with current rent unpaid. Suits to regain possession must start within 90 days, and damage claims within one year.

The security deposit stays your problem after the sale. Under MCL 554.614, a landlord whose interest ends by sale stays liable for the deposit until it is passed to the successor with written notice to the tenant by ordinary mail, until the successor meets the deposit rules, or until the tenant gets it back. Settle it in the closing papers and keep proof of the mailing.

The statute also lets a new owner recover possession by summary proceedings in two sale-related cases: occupants who stay after a mortgage or execution sale once the redemption time has run, and occupants who stay after a personal representative sells under probate court license or will authority (MCL 600.5714(1)(g) and (h)). Beyond those, whether a lease survives a sale depends on the lease text and the notices already served. Check with the clerk of the district court that covers the property, or with a Michigan attorney, before a buyer is told the house will be vacant.

  • Gather the lease, rent ledger, deposit amount, and any notice already served.
  • Pick the notice only after you know which ground applies.
  • Tell the buyer up front whether the house comes occupied or empty.

faqs.q: Is a 7-day notice enough to evict for unpaid rent in Michigan?
faqs.a: It starts the process but doesn't end it. After the 7 days run, the landlord must file in district court, win a judgment for possession, and wait for a writ, which normally can't issue until 10 days after judgment (MCL 600.5744(5)).

faqs.q: Can I end a tenancy at will so I can sell?
faqs.a: Yes, through a notice to quit and then summary proceedings if the tenant stays. A tenancy at will or by sufferance ends on one month's notice, or a period equal to the rent interval when rent is paid more often than every 3 months (MCL 554.134(1)).

faqs.q: Does paying the judgment stop the eviction?
faqs.a: For rent cases, yes, if the full judgment amount and taxed costs are paid to the landlord within the time provided. A writ of restitution can't issue after that payment (MCL 600.5744(7)).

faqs.q: What if the tenant applies for rental assistance?
faqs.a: The case is paused for 14 days when proof of the application is filed and served, and the pause can be extended for 14 more days with a status update. This applies to nonpayment cases.

faqs.q: Who gets the security deposit when the landlord sells?
faqs.a: The seller stays liable until the deposit reaches the buyer and the tenant is told by ordinary mail who the new landlord is and where to write, or until the tenant is repaid (MCL 554.614).
